## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the collection of ambient particulate matter
(PM) on pre-weighed filters using active (pump-based) samplers for
subsequent gravimetric and/or chemical analysis. Gravimetric filter
sampling provides a reference-quality mass concentration that can be
used to validate or calibrate low-cost PM sensors (see
[SOP-F502](SOP-F502-air-quality-portable-sensors.qmd)) and to collect
PM for compositional analysis (metals, ions, elemental/organic carbon)
[@usepa2017frm; @chow1995].

This SOP covers medium- and low-volume filter-based samplers operated
by EA Program personnel. It does not cover Federal Reference Method
(FRM) high-volume samplers operated by regulatory agencies.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Collection of PM~2.5~ and PM~10~ on filters using
  portable or semi-permanent medium-volume or personal air samplers
  (e.g., MiniVol, BGI PQ200, SKC personal samplers) at EA Program
  field sites
- **Does not apply to:** Low-cost optical sensors without filters (see
  [SOP-F502](SOP-F502-air-quality-portable-sensors.qmd)); FRM/FEM
  high-volume samplers operated by AQMD or EPA; indoor air quality
  sampling; gas-phase pollutant sampling
- **Location:** EA Program field deployment sites in the Pomona
  College area and surrounding Inland Empire communities


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling plan, coordinate site access |
| Trained Personnel | Condition filters, deploy sampler, retrieve and weigh filters |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain balance, desiccator, and sampler calibration |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent deployment |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Electrical:** Sampling pumps require AC or battery power. Protect
  connections from rain and moisture.
- **Traffic:** Many monitoring locations are near roadways. Wear a
  high-visibility vest and follow
  [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) traffic safety procedures.
- **Lifting:** Medium-volume samplers (e.g., MiniVol TAS) and
  batteries can be heavy (10--15 kg). Use proper lifting technique.
- **Heat:** Enclosures and pumps can overheat in direct sunlight
  during Inland Empire summers.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling filters)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes
- [ ] High-visibility vest (if near roadways)
- [ ] Sun protection


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Medium-volume sampler (e.g., MiniVol TAS, BGI PQ200) or personal sampler (SKC, Leland Legacy) | With size-selective inlet (PM~2.5~ or PM~10~ impactor) |
| Calibrated flow meter (rotameter or primary standard, e.g., Bios DryCal) | For verifying and adjusting flow rate |
| Timer or elapsed-time indicator       | Built into most samplers       |
| Tripod or mounting pole               | For positioning inlet at breathing zone height (1.5--2 m) |
| Battery or AC power source            | Sufficient for the planned sampling duration |

### Filter Supplies

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Pre-weighed PTFE (Teflon) filters, 47 mm | For gravimetric analysis; inert and low artifact mass |
| Pre-weighed quartz fiber filters, 47 mm | If elemental/organic carbon analysis is planned; pre-fire at 500 C for 4 hours |
| Filter cassettes or holders           | Matched to the sampler         |
| Petri dishes or filter transport cases | For transporting conditioned filters |
| Forceps (flat-tipped, non-serrated)   | For handling filters without touching the deposit |
| Desiccator with active desiccant      | For pre- and post-sampling filter conditioning |
| Analytical balance (0.01 mg or better) | Per [SOP-L200](../lab_sops/SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd) |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Filter Conditioning and Pre-Weighing

1. Place unused filters in a desiccator at controlled temperature
   (20--25 C) and humidity (30--40% RH) for at least 24 hours
   [@usepa2017frm]
2. Weigh each filter on the microbalance to the nearest 0.01 mg.
   Record the filter ID and tare weight.
3. Weigh each filter a second time (at least 1 hour later) to confirm
   stability. The two weights should agree within 0.015 mg.
4. Place the conditioned filter in a labeled Petri dish or cassette.
   Seal and transport in a cooler if traveling to a remote site.

### 6.2 Sampler Setup and Flow Calibration

1. Install the appropriate size-selective inlet (PM~2.5~ or PM~10~
   impactor head) on the sampler
2. Load a blank filter cassette (without the sample filter) and
   connect the calibrated flow meter downstream of the filter holder
3. Start the pump and adjust the flow rate to the nominal design flow
   for the inlet (e.g., 5 L/min for a MiniVol PM~2.5~ impactor)
4. Record the calibrated flow rate, temperature, and barometric
   pressure. If the site is at a different elevation than the
   calibration location, apply a volumetric correction.
5. Remove the blank cassette and load the pre-weighed sample filter
   using forceps. Handle the filter only by its edges.

### 6.3 Deployment

1. Position the sampler with the inlet at 1.5--2 m above ground level,
   unobstructed by walls or overhangs (at least 2 m from any
   vertical surface)
2. Record the start date, start time, site ID, filter ID, GPS
   coordinates, and weather conditions
3. Start the sampler and verify that the pump is running (check the
   flow indicator or elapsed-time counter)
4. For 24-hour integrated samples, allow the sampler to run for
   23--25 hours. For shorter sampling periods (e.g., 8-hour personal
   exposure), record the exact duration.

### 6.4 Retrieval

1. Record the stop time and elapsed run time from the sampler's timer
2. Verify the flow rate with the calibrated flow meter before stopping
   the pump (post-sampling flow check). Record the value.
3. Stop the pump
4. Remove the filter cassette using gloves. Transfer the exposed
   filter to its labeled Petri dish or transport case using forceps.
   Do not touch the deposit surface.
5. Seal the Petri dish and place in a cooler for transport to the
   laboratory
6. Calculate the average flow rate: $Q_{\text{avg}} = (Q_{\text{pre}}
   + Q_{\text{post}}) / 2$. If the pre- and post-flow rates differ by
   more than 10%, flag the sample.

### 6.5 Post-Sampling Conditioning and Weighing

1. Condition the exposed filter in the same desiccator and at the same
   temperature/humidity as the pre-weighing step for at least 24 hours
2. Weigh the filter to the nearest 0.01 mg. Record the gross weight.
3. Repeat the weighing at least 1 hour later to confirm stability.
4. Calculate the net PM mass:

   $$
   m_{\text{PM}} = W_{\text{post}} - W_{\text{pre}}
   $$

5. Calculate the PM concentration:

   $$
   C_{\text{PM}} (\mu\text{g/m}^3) = \frac{m_{\text{PM}} (\mu\text{g})}{Q_{\text{avg}} (\text{L/min}) \times t (\text{min})} \times 10^3
   $$

### 6.6 Filter Archiving and Downstream Analysis

1. After gravimetric analysis, archive filters in sealed Petri dishes
   at room temperature (or at -20 C if chemical analysis is planned)
2. For elemental/organic carbon analysis, submit quartz filters to the
   analytical laboratory per their instructions
3. For metals analysis by XRF or ICP-MS, submit PTFE filters per
   [SOP-L205](../lab_sops/SOP-L205-xrf-sample-prep-analysis.qmd) or
   [SOP-L410](../lab_sops/SOP-L410-hotplate-acid-digestion.qmd)


## 7. Quality Control

- Collect at least one field blank per sampling event: load a
  conditioned filter into a cassette, transport it to the site, open
  the cassette briefly (without running the pump), seal, and return
  to the lab for conditioning and weighing
- Collect duplicate samples (co-located samplers) for at least 10% of
  sampling events. Duplicate PM concentrations should agree within 15%.
- Verify the balance with NIST-traceable check weights at the start of
  each weighing session
- Document pre- and post-sampling flow rates; flag samples where the
  difference exceeds 10%
- Re-condition and re-weigh at least 10% of filters as laboratory
  duplicates; agreement should be within 0.015 mg


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Exposed PTFE or quartz filters (after analysis) | Standard trash (non-hazardous) |
| Impactor grease and oiled impaction substrates | Chemical waste; EH&S pickup |
| Used desiccant                | Standard trash or regenerate per manufacturer |

## 11. Training Record

Before deploying PM samplers independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate proper filter handling (forceps, desiccator,
   conditioning, weighing) under supervision
3. Perform a flow calibration and sampler setup under supervision
4. Deploy and retrieve a sampler for one complete sampling period
   with acceptable QC results (field blank mass within 0.015 mg of
   pre-weight; pre/post flow agreement within 10%)
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
